title: Simple
coreMove: compress the plan until the people under pressure can repeat the intent, sequence, and constraints from memory
sourcePressure: Overcomplicated plans and explanations collapse under pressure; simple plans survive chaos because people can understand and execute them.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: simple means dumbed down or underplanned
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

counterintuition: leadership is harder than it looks
tryThisNow: ask yourself how to be a better leader

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: campground wildfire evacuation notice for weekend campers
exampleSpecs.audience: a park superintendent whose draft plan has six color-coded zones
exampleSpecs.stakes: families may not remember the route when smoke lowers visibility
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the superintendent replaces the color code with three named exits, has a seasonal ranger repeat the plan back, and cuts any step the ranger cannot say cleanly
exampleSpecs.firstImage: ash flecks land on a laminated campground map at the ranger kiosk
mustAvoid: oversimplifying into vague stay safe advice

exampleSpecs.domain: pharmacy recall instruction for a crowded neighborhood counter
exampleSpecs.audience: a pharmacist explaining a medication recall to technicians and patients
exampleSpecs.stakes: confusing directions can send patients home with the wrong bottles
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the pharmacist rewrites the recall into three bins and one patient sentence, then asks the newest tech to process a sample return
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are close enough to see this: orange recall stickers scatter beside three empty plastic bins.

exampleSpecs.domain: software incident runbook during a payment outage
exampleSpecs.audience: an incident commander with engineers arguing over twelve tabs of instructions
exampleSpecs.stakes: customers cannot pay while the team debates which procedure applies
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the commander closes the extra tabs, names one rollback path, one customer message, and one owner for each, then has the room repeat it
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The first thing you register is physical: checkout error graph spikes red beside twelve open browser tabs.

exampleSpecs.domain: wedding venue rain switch with an anxious couple waiting
exampleSpecs.audience: an event captain leading servers, florist, and musicians
exampleSpecs.stakes: a complex contingency sheet can collapse during the thirty-minute weather pivot
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the captain cuts the rain plan to aisle, chairs, music, and guest path, assigns one owner to each, and refuses a decorative change that would confuse the move
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Hold there," someone says. Raindrops darken the edge of a printed seating chart on the ceremony table.

exampleSpecs.audience: a dive instructor with nervous students overloaded by safety detail
exampleSpecs.stakes: students must remember the emergency sequence underwater
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the instructor reduces the drill to stop, signal, breathe, ascend, then has each student demonstrate it with a pressure gauge before entering open water
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Later, the team will trace the lesson back to this: pressure gauge needle rests in the red while fins slap against the dock.

exampleSpecs.domain: animal shelter intake after a hoarding seizure
exampleSpecs.audience: a shelter director with volunteers facing thirty incoming cats
exampleSpecs.stakes: unclear intake steps can lose medical notes and separate bonded animals
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director replaces a long intake packet with four station cards, walks the first carrier through them, and stops when a volunteer cannot explain station three
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What changes once this is in front of everyone: cardboard cat carrier scratches against a folding intake table?

skillTargets: compress a plan without stripping the essential constraints
use repeat-back as the pressure test for simplicity
reject impressive complexity that frontline people cannot execute

tryThisNowSpec: Take a plan you own and reduce it to intent, three steps, and two limits; ask someone new to repeat it back.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
